### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 169ff7e53889d275c7db1b1bd0e22e37791c58df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `714f5e0f6d7e577dd70b00857bcc240ee2765fe1` — the merge of head `ab2845c82053c7e6d35286e2c7cd7713145b5dee` into base `169ff7e53889d275c7db1b1bd0e22e37791c58df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 714f5e0f6d7e577dd70b00857bcc240ee2765fe1 && git checkout 714f5e0f6d7e577dd70b00857bcc240ee2765fe1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 169ff7e53889d275c7db1b1bd0e22e37791c58df ab2845c82053c7e6d35286e2c7cd7713145b5dee && git checkout -B drift-repro 169ff7e53889d275c7db1b1bd0e22e37791c58df && git merge --no-ff ab2845c82053c7e6d35286e2c7cd7713145b5dee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 169ff7e53889d275c7db1b1bd0e22e37791c58df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 169ff7e53889d275c7db1b1bd0e22e37791c58df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#5 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5o8PE7ZtVjcor51wBZ

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:服务优雅关闭(`HonoHttpServer.close()`)时,一个已经调用 `end()`、但还在往慢客户端发送的响应,不再在关闭开始那一刻被掐断;空闲的 keep-alive 连接改为在没有响应仍在发送时才统一释放。
- 为什么改:每次 `os serve` / 运行时关停或重新部署时,正在下载大响应的客户端会收到被截断的内容(实测 32 MiB 只收到 3,919,702 字节),原因是 Node 自己的 `server.close()` 把「已 end 未发完」的连接当作空闲连接销毁了。
- 风险与回滚:只改 `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` 一个文件,patch 级;关闭窗口的强制关闭兜底(默认 10 秒)原样保留,所以最坏情况是空闲连接晚一点释放,不会让关停卡住;回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts` 的 `closeIdleConnectionsOnceFlushed`(什么时候推迟清扫),再看 `tryListen` 里把它装到 server 实例上的那三行,以及 `trackForDrain` 里响应 `'close'` 时补跑被推迟的清扫。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run src/adapter-drain.test.ts`,预期 9 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

席位意见:接受。优雅关闭时,已结束但还在往慢客户端发送的响应不再被 Node 的空闲连接清理截断;清理改为等所有在发送的响应发完再跑,排空窗口的强制关闭兜底不变。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:server#5` · Head-sha `ab2845c82053c7e6d35286e2c7cd7713145b5dee` · 2026-11-07T20:32Z

- **Shape:** 3 files, +151/−11, read from the diff. `adapter.ts`: the server instance's `closeIdleConnections` is wrapped (so Node's own `server.close()` → `httpServerPreClose` reaches the wrapper too) by `closeIdleConnectionsOnceFlushed`, which holds the sweep while any tracked response is `writableEnded && !writableFinished` and re-runs it from `trackForDrain`'s `'close'` handler; `deferredIdleSweep` is cleared on close. The force-close backstop is unchanged.
- **Premise measured:** on Node 22 Node's `server.close()` sweep destroys the flushing socket first, the adapter's own call second (dev reading); the reordered slow-reader pin is red on main `df22adc3` (`expected 3919702 to be 33554432`).
- **Pins:** reordered slow-reader case gets every byte (ablated red, restored); CONTROL idle keep-alive still closes at drain start; CONTROL backstop still force-closes a reader that never drains.
- **Gates:** head check-runs 35 `success`, 13 skipped, none red or pending. `Test Core (8/8)` was red once on this head: two `examples/app-todo` `loop-body-iteration.test.ts` cases timed out at 5000 ms inside `bootTodoKernel` (no HTTP server in that test, nothing this diff reaches); re-run once by the seat, green. `check-expected-skips`: OK, all 13 in main's roster (exit 0). No governed path. The dev's `dispatch-gates --commands`: 63 derived, 63 run, all exit 0. Mergeable state `clean`.
- **Accepted deviations:** none beyond the order.
- **Out of scope:** none. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs:` n/a. Changeset `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` patch.
- **Landing:** ungoverned. `Fixes #31208`. Ready + auto-merge.
